# data/firebase-open-rules

Firebase rules open to everyone.

firestore.rules or storage.rules with `allow read, write: if true`, `allow write: if true`, or the test-mode rule `if request.time < timestamp.date(...)`; database.rules.json with ".write": true.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: block for public writes and for a public read of the whole Firestore database; warn for public reads of a specific path or a whole Storage bucket, public create-only rules on a specific path, writes open to any signed-in user on the whole database, a root ".read": true in database.rules.json, and everything under example and template folders. Rules under test folders are skipped.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-284](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html), [CWE-862](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/862.html), OWASP A01:2025.

## Why it matters

Firebase clients talk to the database directly with a public config, so the rules are the only access control. Open or test-mode rules let anyone read, change, or delete the data.

## Flagged

`apps/site/firestore.rules` (block):

```text
allow read: if true;
```

`apps/site/firestore.rules` (warn):

```text
allow write: if request.auth != null;
```

`examples/chat/firestore.rules` (warn):

```text
allow read, write: if true;
```

`firestore.rules` (block):

```text
allow update, delete: if true;
```

`firestore.rules` (warn):

```text
allow create: if true;
```

`firestore.rules` (block):

```text
allow read, write: if request.time < timestamp.date(2026, 10, 1);
```

`storage.rules` (warn):

```text
allow read;
```

`storage.rules` (block):

```text
allow write: if true;
```

## Not flagged

- `allow read: if resource.data.visible == true;` in `apps/site/firestore.rules`: reads limited to visible comments
- `allow update: if request.auth.uid != null && request.auth.uid == resource.data.author;` in `apps/site/firestore.rules`: author check
- `allow update: if request.auth.uid != null;` in `apps/site/firestore.rules`: signed-in writes on one path are not reported
- `allow read, write: if isOwner(userId);` in `firestore.rules`: owner check through a function
- `allow create: if request.auth != null;` in `firestore.rules`: any signed-in user may create a post on this path
- `allow read, write: if false;` in `firestore.rules`: closed
- `allow read: if request.auth != null;` in `firestore.rules`: reads for signed-in users on one path
- `&& request.resource.data.keys().hasOnly(['name', 'bio']);` in `firestore.rules`: owner check across two lines
- `allow read, write: if request.auth != null && request.auth.uid == userId;` in `storage.rules`: owner check
- `allow read, write: if true;` in `test/emulator/firestore.rules`: emulator rules under a test folder are not deployed

## How to fix

Replace the condition with a check on the signed-in user, such as `request.auth != null && request.auth.uid == userId`, and deny everything else.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore data/firebase-open-rules: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "data/firebase-open-rules": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).
